citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the transverse space $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]], with $P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$ for $\mathbf k\ne0$ and any assigned value at the null point $\mathbf k=0$. In the QFT length convention, assign $\mathbf k$ units m$^{-1}$ and define the nonnegative measurable multiplier
$$ \omega(\mathbf k):=|\mathbf k|. $$
Its maximal multiplication operator on $\mathcal H_T$ is
$$ (M_\omega f)(\mathbf k):=\omega(\mathbf k)f(\mathbf k),\qquad D(M_\omega):=\{f\in\mathcal H_T:\omega f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)\}. $$
Because $\omega$ is a scalar multiplier, $\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e. implies $\mathbf k\cdot(M_\omega f)(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e.; thus the displayed multiplication maps its stated domain into $\mathcal H_T$. The value $\omega(0)=0$ is immaterial to the $L^2$ operator. For $\hbar,c>0$, the corresponding one-particle energy convention is $E_1:=\hbar c M_\omega$, in joules.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite measure space and let
$\boldsymbol\omega=(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_d):X\to\mathbb R^d$ be a
finite-valued measurable map, where $d\ge1$. Put
$H=L^2(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ with the second-variable-linear pairing of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], and form the bosonic Fock space
$\mathcal F_s(H)$. For $n\ge1$, identify $H_s^{(n)}$ with the symmetric
subspace of $L^2(X^n,\overline{\mu^{\times n}};\mathbb C)$ by iterating
[[lem-qft-l2-product-tensor-identification]]. Set $X^0=\{\star\}$,
$s_0(\star)=0$, and for $n\ge1$ set
$$s_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{r=1}^n\boldsymbol\omega(x_r)\in\mathbb R^d.$$
For $1\le j\le d$, define $H_j$ by multiplication by the $j$th coordinate
$s_{n,j}$ on sector $n$, with exact domain
$$D(H_j)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n): \sum_{n\ge1}\int_{X^n}|s_{n,j}|^2|\Psi_n|^2\,d\overline{\mu^{\times n}}<\infty\right\}.$$
Each $H_j$ is self-adjoint, and $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\cap D(H_j)$ is a
graph core. The joint projection-valued measure
[[def-projection-valued-measure]] on $\mathbb R^d$ is
$$(E(B)\Psi)_n=\mathbf1_{s_n^{-1}(B)}\Psi_n\quad(n\ge1),\qquad (E(B)\Psi)_0=\mathbf1_B(0)\Psi_0.$$
For $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, let $H_\theta$ be multiplication on sector $n$
by $\theta\cdot s_n$, with its maximal square-integrability domain. Then
$$U_\theta(t)\Psi:=\bigl(e^{it\theta\cdot s_n}\Psi_n\bigr)_{n\ge0}$$
is a strongly continuous unitary group on all of Fock space, and its norm
derivative at zero exists exactly for $\Psi\in D(H_\theta)$, where it is
$iH_\theta\Psi$. The zero-particle sector is the vacuum eigenvector at joint
value $0$.

For an integer $d\ge1$, let $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ be the complex Schwartz space with seminorms
$p_{\alpha\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$
for all multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$; this is exactly
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]. Let
$\mathcal D(\mathbb R^d)=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ with the support convention of
[[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]] and the locally convex LF topology of
[[def-test-function-topology]]. The tempered-distribution space $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^d)$
is the space of continuous complex-linear functionals on this topological
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, paired bilinearly with test functions, as in
[[def-tempered-distribution]].

For every complex Hilbert space $H$, use the second-variable-linear pairing
$\langle u,v\rangle_2:=(v,u)_1$, where $(\cdot,\cdot)_1$ is the first-variable-linear
Hilbert pairing of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]. Thus
$\langle u,v\rangle_2$ is linear in $v$ and conjugate-linear in $u$.
For each tensor product, use the same norm completion as
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], but equip it with the
second-variable-linear pairing obtained by conjugating that supplier's
first-variable-linear pairing. This leaves the norm and completion unchanged;
on elementary tensors it gives the product of the second-variable pairings.
Let $H^{\widehat\otimes n}$ be the iterated Hilbert tensor completion, with
$H^{\widehat\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$; the tensor inner product is the product of
the factor pairings. For $n\ge1$, let
$P_{s,n}=n!^{-1}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi$ and
$P_{a,n}=n!^{-1}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$, using the
permutation action and the orthogonal projections of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. Define
$H_s^{(n)}=\operatorname{ran}P_{s,n}$ and
$H_a^{(n)}=\operatorname{ran}P_{a,n}$, with
$H_s^{(0)}=H_a^{(0)}=\mathbb C$. These are the symmetric and antisymmetric
$n$-particle sectors.

The bosonic and fermionic Fock Hilbert spaces are the square-summable direct
sums
$\mathcal F_s(H)=\{(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\Psi_n\in H_s^{(n)},\
\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$ and
$\mathcal F_a(H)=\{(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\Psi_n\in H_a^{(n)},\
\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, with the componentwise inner product.
Their vacuum is $\Omega=(1,0,0,\ldots)$. The finite-particle subspace
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ consists of sequences with only finitely many nonzero
components.

For $n\ge0$, bosonic creation on sector $n$ is
$a_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}P_{s,n+1}(h\otimes\Psi_n)$; for $n\ge1$,
bosonic annihilation is
$a_n(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt n(C_h\otimes I^{\otimes(n-1)})\Psi_n$, where
$C_h(v)=\langle h,v\rangle_2$ and its tensor extension is the bounded map of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], and $a(h)\Omega=0$. Define fermionic creation
by $c_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}P_{a,n+1}(h\otimes\Psi_n)$; for $n\ge1$,
fermionic annihilation is the corresponding first-factor contraction
$c_n(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt n(C_h\otimes I^{\otimes(n-1)})\Psi_n$, and
$c(h)\Omega=0$. The annihilation maps are conjugate-linear in $h$; the
creation maps are linear in $h$. These formulas define sector maps on the
finite-particle subspace; their maximal closed domains and operator relations are proved in
[[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. No physical statistics assignment or spin–statistics
theorem is part of these mathematical definitions.

Assume the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Let S be a compact embedded $C^1$ hypersurface in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$. Choose finitely many regular injective $C^1$ parametrizations $X_j:V_j\to S\cap O_j$ with $C^1$ coordinate transitions, and an ambient partition $\chi_j$ from [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]], with supports compactly contained in the corresponding chart neighborhoods. Put $J_{X_j}=\sqrt{\det(DX_j^TDX_j)}$, using [[def-gram-matrix-and-gram-determinant]].

For a nonnegative Borel f on S define $\int_S f\,dS=\sum_j\int_{V_j}(\chi_j f)(X_j(y))J_{X_j}(y)\,dy$, where the integrals on the right are those of [[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]] and $0\cdot\infty=0$. Set $S(A)=\int_S\mathbf1_A\,dS$ for Borel A. For signed f with $\int_S|f|\,dS<\infty$ use the difference of the positive and negative integrals. The same chart formula restricts to a compact Borel face contained in a regular patch. The empty surface has zero integral. Independence and finiteness are established by the following chart-independence lemma.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and $n\ge2$. The chart surface measure on $S^{n-1}$ equals the polar measure $\sigma$. Orthogonal transformations preserve it. The map $\omega\mapsto a+R\omega$, $R>0$, multiplies surface measure by $R^{n-1}$, and $|S^{n-1}|=n|B_1|$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n \ge 1$,
let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be the unit sphere, and let $\sigma$ be the
set function of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. Then $\sigma$
is a finite Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$, and for every Borel measurable
$f : \mathbb R^n \to [0,\infty]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)\,d\lambda_n(x) = \int_0^\infty \int_{S^{n-1}} f(r\omega) r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr.$$
Moreover, $\sigma$ is the unique Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ with this
property.

Let $\iota_{\mathbb R}\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be the canonical-natural map
of [[def-canonical-natural]], and let $j\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be the real
embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every
$n\in\mathbb N$, the factorial $n!$ is nonzero by
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], so
$\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!)>0$ by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and consequently
$j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))\ne0$ in the complex field
[[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]].

For $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$
whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we
abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the
same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a
natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of
[[def-complex-integer-powers]] and
[[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence
for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by
[[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]].
For every $z\in\mathbb C$, the series $\sum z^n/n!$ converges absolutely.

For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$, $\exp(z+w)=\exp z\exp w$. For real $x$, the complex value $\exp(x+0i)$ equals the published real exponential $e^x$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]], [[lem-cauchy-product-of-absolutely-convergent-complex-series]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[lem-binomial-theorem-over-complex-numbers]], [[thm-binomial-closed-formula]].

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

For $x>0$, $\log$ is differentiable and
$$\log'(x)=\frac1x,\qquad \log x=\int_1^x\frac{dt}{t}.$$

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

derivations.claim: For $\mathbf n\in S^2$, $P_T(\mathbf n)=I-\mathbf n\mathbf n^\top$ is an orthogonal projection and [A2] gives $\mathbf n\cdot b(\mathbf n)=0$; hence $\mathbf k\cdot f_\epsilon(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e. Since $\epsilon<|\mathbf k|<\kappa$ on the support, the radial norm integrals in [F4]–[F6] are finite on these strictly positive finite bounds, so both $f_\epsilon$ and $\omega f_\epsilon$ are square-integrable.

By [F4]–[F6], spherical coordinates give $d^3k=r^2dr\,d\Omega$. Substituting $r=\epsilon u$ in the radial integral and using [F10] gives $\int_\epsilon^\kappa dr/r=\log(\kappa/\epsilon)$, so $\|f_\epsilon\|^2=C_b\int_\epsilon^\kappa r^{-1}dr=C_b\log(\kappa/\epsilon)$, $\langle f_\epsilon,\omega f_\epsilon\rangle=C_b(\kappa-\epsilon)$, and $\|\omega f_\epsilon\|^2=C_b(\kappa^2-\epsilon^2)/2$.

For any $u,v\in\mathcal H_T$, [F2] gives $\langle u^{\otimes n},v^{\otimes n}\rangle=\langle u,v\rangle^n$ and $\|u^{\otimes n}\|^2=\|u\|^{2n}$. By [F7]–[F8], $\sum_{n\ge0}\|u\|^{2n}/n!=e^{\|u\|^2}<\infty$, so the displayed $\epsilon(u)$ belongs to symmetric Fock space. Its direct-sum pairing with $\epsilon(v)$ is the absolutely convergent series $\sum_{n\ge0}\langle u,v\rangle^n/n!=e^{\langle u,v\rangle}$, by [F7]. The addition and modulus laws [F8]–[F9] therefore give that $C(u)$ has norm one and $|\langle C(u),C(v)\rangle|=e^{-\|u-v\|^2/2}$. This direct tensor calculation requires no separability hypothesis on $\mathcal H_T$. On the full vector space $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, multiplication by $\omega$ commutes with the multiplier $P_T$. Its tensor-power projections therefore commute with the sector multiplier $\sum_j|\mathbf k_j|$; the transverse symmetric Fock space is a reducing subspace for the second-quantized multiplier of [F3]. If $r=\|f_\epsilon\|^2$, $q=\langle f_\epsilon,\omega f_\epsilon\rangle$, and $s=\|\omega f_\epsilon\|^2$, the sector formulas give
$$ \|d\Gamma(\omega)C(f_\epsilon)\|^2 =e^{-r}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n s r^{n-1}+n(n-1)q^2r^{n-2}}{n!} =s+q^2<\infty. $$
The same sector sum with one multiplier gives $\langle C(f_\epsilon),d\Gamma(\omega)C(f_\epsilon)\rangle=q$; [F2] gives $\|C(f_\epsilon)\|=1$. Multiplying by $\hbar c$ and substituting [step 1.2] proves the stated domain and energy claims.

Put $\epsilon_j=\kappa 2^{-j}$ for $j\ge1$. The difference $f_{\epsilon_{j+1}}-f_{\epsilon_j}$ is supported on the shell $(\epsilon_{j+1},\epsilon_j)$, so its squared norm is $C_b\int_{\epsilon_{j+1}}^{\epsilon_j}r^{-1}dr=C_b\log2>0$, using $r=\epsilon_{j+1}u$ and [F10]. From the pairing identity in step 2.1,
$$ |\langle C(f_{\epsilon_j}),C(f_{\epsilon_{j+1}})\rangle| =e^{-\|f_{\epsilon_{j+1}}-f_{\epsilon_j}\|^2/2}=e^{-C_b\log2/2}<1. $$
Thus $\|C(f_{\epsilon_j})-C(f_{\epsilon_{j+1}})\|^2\ge2(1-e^{-C_b\log2/2})>0$, and this sequence is not Cauchy.

Let $\Psi$ have only sectors $0,\ldots,N$. By sectorwise Cauchy–Schwarz [F11],
$$ |\langle\Psi,C(f_\epsilon)\rangle| \le e^{-\|f_\epsilon\|^2/2}\sum_{n=0}^{N}\frac{\|\Psi_n\|\|f_\epsilon\|^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\longrightarrow0 $$
as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, as follows explicitly. If $\epsilon<\kappa2^{-m}$, the radial integral in
step 1.2 contains $m$ disjoint dyadic intervals; on each $(a,2a)$,
$\int_a^{2a}dr/r\ge1/2$. Thus $\|f_\epsilon\|^2\ge C_bm/2\to\infty$.
Write $a=\|f_\epsilon\|$ and choose an integer $M>N/2$. The nonnegative
real exponential series [F7]–[F8] gives
$e^{a^2/2}\ge(a^2/2)^M/M!$. Hence for $0\le n\le N$,
$a^ne^{-a^2/2}\le2^MM!a^{n-2M}\to0$, proving the displayed finite-sum limit. Finite-sector vectors are dense: for any Fock vector $\Psi=(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}$, the truncations $\sum_{n=0}^N\Psi_n$ converge in norm because $\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty$. Since $\|C(f_\epsilon)\|=1$, [F11] bounds the pairing of each truncation error by its norm, uniformly in $\epsilon$. First taking a sufficiently accurate truncation and then the limit just proved gives weak convergence to zero for every Fock vector. A norm limit would have to equal the weak limit zero, contradicting the unit norms.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the transverse space $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]], with $P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$ for $\mathbf k\ne0$ and any assigned value at the null point $\mathbf k=0$. In the QFT length convention, assign $\mathbf k$ units m$^{-1}$ and define the nonnegative measurable multiplier
$$ \omega(\mathbf k):=|\mathbf k|. $$
Its maximal multiplication operator on $\mathcal H_T$ is
$$ (M_\omega f)(\mathbf k):=\omega(\mathbf k)f(\mathbf k),\qquad D(M_\omega):=\{f\in\mathcal H_T:\omega f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)\}. $$
Because $\omega$ is a scalar multiplier, $\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e. implies $\mathbf k\cdot(M_\omega f)(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e.; thus the displayed multiplication maps its stated domain into $\mathcal H_T$. The value $\omega(0)=0$ is immaterial to the $L^2$ operator. For $\hbar,c>0$, the corresponding one-particle energy convention is $E_1:=\hbar c M_\omega$, in joules.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite measure space and let
$\boldsymbol\omega=(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_d):X\to\mathbb R^d$ be a
finite-valued measurable map, where $d\ge1$. Put
$H=L^2(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ with the second-variable-linear pairing of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], and form the bosonic Fock space
$\mathcal F_s(H)$. For $n\ge1$, identify $H_s^{(n)}$ with the symmetric
subspace of $L^2(X^n,\overline{\mu^{\times n}};\mathbb C)$ by iterating
[[lem-qft-l2-product-tensor-identification]]. Set $X^0=\{\star\}$,
$s_0(\star)=0$, and for $n\ge1$ set
$$s_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{r=1}^n\boldsymbol\omega(x_r)\in\mathbb R^d.$$
For $1\le j\le d$, define $H_j$ by multiplication by the $j$th coordinate
$s_{n,j}$ on sector $n$, with exact domain
$$D(H_j)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n): \sum_{n\ge1}\int_{X^n}|s_{n,j}|^2|\Psi_n|^2\,d\overline{\mu^{\times n}}<\infty\right\}.$$
Each $H_j$ is self-adjoint, and $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\cap D(H_j)$ is a
graph core. The joint projection-valued measure
[[def-projection-valued-measure]] on $\mathbb R^d$ is
$$(E(B)\Psi)_n=\mathbf1_{s_n^{-1}(B)}\Psi_n\quad(n\ge1),\qquad (E(B)\Psi)_0=\mathbf1_B(0)\Psi_0.$$
For $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, let $H_\theta$ be multiplication on sector $n$
by $\theta\cdot s_n$, with its maximal square-integrability domain. Then
$$U_\theta(t)\Psi:=\bigl(e^{it\theta\cdot s_n}\Psi_n\bigr)_{n\ge0}$$
is a strongly continuous unitary group on all of Fock space, and its norm
derivative at zero exists exactly for $\Psi\in D(H_\theta)$, where it is
$iH_\theta\Psi$. The zero-particle sector is the vacuum eigenvector at joint
value $0$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
For an integer $d\ge1$, let $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ be the complex Schwartz space with seminorms
$p_{\alpha\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$
for all multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$; this is exactly
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]. Let
$\mathcal D(\mathbb R^d)=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ with the support convention of
[[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]] and the locally convex LF topology of
[[def-test-function-topology]]. The tempered-distribution space $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^d)$
is the space of continuous complex-linear functionals on this topological
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, paired bilinearly with test functions, as in
[[def-tempered-distribution]].

For every complex Hilbert space $H$, use the second-variable-linear pairing
$\langle u,v\rangle_2:=(v,u)_1$, where $(\cdot,\cdot)_1$ is the first-variable-linear
Hilbert pairing of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]. Thus
$\langle u,v\rangle_2$ is linear in $v$ and conjugate-linear in $u$.
For each tensor product, use the same norm completion as
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], but equip it with the
second-variable-linear pairing obtained by conjugating that supplier's
first-variable-linear pairing. This leaves the norm and completion unchanged;
on elementary tensors it gives the product of the second-variable pairings.
Let $H^{\widehat\otimes n}$ be the iterated Hilbert tensor completion, with
$H^{\widehat\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$; the tensor inner product is the product of
the factor pairings. For $n\ge1$, let
$P_{s,n}=n!^{-1}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi$ and
$P_{a,n}=n!^{-1}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$, using the
permutation action and the orthogonal projections of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. Define
$H_s^{(n)}=\operatorname{ran}P_{s,n}$ and
$H_a^{(n)}=\operatorname{ran}P_{a,n}$, with
$H_s^{(0)}=H_a^{(0)}=\mathbb C$. These are the symmetric and antisymmetric
$n$-particle sectors.

The bosonic and fermionic Fock Hilbert spaces are the square-summable direct
sums
$\mathcal F_s(H)=\{(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\Psi_n\in H_s^{(n)},\
\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$ and
$\mathcal F_a(H)=\{(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\Psi_n\in H_a^{(n)},\
\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, with the componentwise inner product.
Their vacuum is $\Omega=(1,0,0,\ldots)$. The finite-particle subspace
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ consists of sequences with only finitely many nonzero
components.

For $n\ge0$, bosonic creation on sector $n$ is
$a_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}P_{s,n+1}(h\otimes\Psi_n)$; for $n\ge1$,
bosonic annihilation is
$a_n(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt n(C_h\otimes I^{\otimes(n-1)})\Psi_n$, where
$C_h(v)=\langle h,v\rangle_2$ and its tensor extension is the bounded map of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], and $a(h)\Omega=0$. Define fermionic creation
by $c_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}P_{a,n+1}(h\otimes\Psi_n)$; for $n\ge1$,
fermionic annihilation is the corresponding first-factor contraction
$c_n(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt n(C_h\otimes I^{\otimes(n-1)})\Psi_n$, and
$c(h)\Omega=0$. The annihilation maps are conjugate-linear in $h$; the
creation maps are linear in $h$. These formulas define sector maps on the
finite-particle subspace; their maximal closed domains and operator relations are proved in
[[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. No physical statistics assignment or spin–statistics
theorem is part of these mathematical definitions.

For a nonnegative Borel f on S define $\int_S f\,dS=\sum_j\int_{V_j}(\chi_j f)(X_j(y))J_{X_j}(y)\,dy$, where the integrals on the right are those of [[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]] and $0\cdot\infty=0$. supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n \ge 1$,
let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be the unit sphere, and let $\sigma$ be the
set function of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. Then $\sigma$
is a finite Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$, and for every Borel measurable
$f : \mathbb R^n \to [0,\infty]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)\,d\lambda_n(x) = \int_0^\infty \int_{S^{n-1}} f(r\omega) r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr.$$
Moreover, $\sigma$ is the unique Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ with this
property.

embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every

[[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]].

For $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$
whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we
abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the
same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a
natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of
[[def-complex-integer-powers]] and
[[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence
for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by

citations.quote: Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], the mathematical scalar shell conventions of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], and the second-variable-linear Hilbert pairing of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. In the fixed inertial coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] on the affine Minkowski model [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; these coordinates have length units under [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. The parameter $\mu\ge0$ and momentum coordinate $\mathbf k$ have inverse-length units, and $\omega(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$ has the same units. The parameter is not identified here with a physical rest mass. Matrix $h_D$ has inverse-length units; the dimensionless spin matrices have no physical unit assignment in this mathematical item.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

Use the Pauli matrices $\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. On $\mathbb C^4=\mathbb C^2\oplus\mathbb C^2$, define
$$\beta=\begin{pmatrix}I_2&0\\0&-I_2\end{pmatrix},\qquad \alpha_j=\begin{pmatrix}0&\sigma_j\\\sigma_j&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \gamma^0=\beta,\qquad \gamma^j=\beta\alpha_j.$$
For a spinor column $z\in\mathbb C^4$, its Dirac adjoint is $\bar z=z^\dagger\beta$. The Clifford contraction is $\Gamma(p):=\gamma^0p^0-\sum_{j=1}^3\gamma^jp_j$; this contraction uses the effective matrix $-\eta$ in the relation $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Here
$\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ is the Schwartz space of smooth complex functions
whose coordinate-weighted derivatives are all bounded, as defined in
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]].
Fix an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space and an inertial coordinate
chart as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use coordinates
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ and metric $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, matching the
$(-+++)$ convention of the SR suppliers. Some QFT sources use its negative
$(+---)$; the Lorentz group is unchanged, and the phase is fixed explicitly
below.
Coordinates $x$ have length units, momenta have inverse-length units, and the
Fourier phase below is dimensionless. A parameter $\mu\ge0$ has inverse-length
units and is only a mathematical shell parameter; it is not identified with a
physical rest mass. For $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, set
$$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2},\qquad p_\mu(\mathbf k)=(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k).$$
The future mass shell is
$$H_\mu^+=\{(p^0,\mathbf p): (p^0)^2-|\mathbf p|^2=\mu^2,\ p^0>0\}.$$
When $\mu=0$, its apex is omitted; thus $\mathbf k\ne0$ in the massless
parameterization. The scalar shell pairing is
$$p\circ x:=p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$
Define the measure and one-particle Hilbert space by
$$d\nu_\mu(p_\mu(\mathbf k))= \frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)},\qquad H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C),$$
where the omitted massless apex has measure zero. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb
R^4)$ define its pointwise shell Fourier restriction by
$$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x.$$
The Fourier convention is exactly the displayed integral, with no prefactor.
If $\widehat f(\xi^0,\boldsymbol\xi)=
\int f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x^0\xi^0+\mathbf x\cdot\boldsymbol\xi)}\,d^4x$ denotes
the standard transform in
[[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]],
then
$$\mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p):=\int f(x)e^{i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)}\,d^4x =\widehat f\!\left(-\frac{p^0}{2\pi},\frac{\mathbf p}{2\pi}\right).$$
Its inverse is
$$f(x)=(2\pi)^{-4}\int_{\mathbb R^4} \mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p)e^{-i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)} \,dp^0\,d^3\mathbf p.$$
Thus this convention is a time reflection and rescaling of the cited
Schwartz automorphism and has the stated reciprocal normalization.
The proper orthochronous Lorentz group consists of linear maps preserving
$\eta$, orientation and the chosen future cone. A Poincare map is
$x\mapsto a+\Lambda x$ with $a\in\mathbb R^4$ and $\Lambda$ in that group.

This is a mathematical free scalar one-particle construction. It adopts the
chosen coordinates, measure and Fourier convention; it asserts no experimental
observation, physical mass identification or measurement outcome.

Let $K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)$ and $S(z;\zeta)$ be the finite-dimensional formal matrices of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]], with $d\ge1$, $K_0(\zeta)$ invertible, and both coefficient matrices covariant under the vertex phase angles of [[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Then $S$ is a two-sided inverse of $K$ in $M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$, and
$$ S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1} $$
coefficientwise. For a real vertex tuple $\theta$, put
$\Theta:=\operatorname{diag}_{x\in X}(\theta_xI_r)$,
$\zeta_s:=\zeta^{s\theta}$, and $D_s:=D_{s\theta}=e^{is\Theta}$.
Write $K_s:=K(z;\zeta_s)$ and $S_s:=S(z;\zeta_s)$, and define
$\delta K:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}K_s\right|_{s=0}$ and
$\delta S:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}S_s\right|_{s=0}$ coefficientwise along this
differentiable phase path. The variations satisfy
$$ \delta K=i[\Theta,K],\qquad \delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S . $$
For ordinary finite matrices $A,B\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$, the corresponding resolvent identity is $B^{-1}(B-A)A^{-1}=A^{-1}-B^{-1}$. These are formal or finite algebraic statements; they assert no convergence of a perturbation series, continuum limit, or loop Ward identity.

derivations.claim: From the displayed Pauli matrices in [F1], direct multiplication gives $\sigma_j^\dagger=\sigma_j$, $\sigma_j^2=I_2$, and $\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=0$ for $i\ne j$. The block formulas then give $\beta^2=I_4$, $\beta^\dagger=\beta$, $\gamma^{0\dagger}=\gamma^0$, $\gamma^{j\dagger}=-\gamma^j$, and $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=2h^{ab}I_4$. Consequently $\Gamma(p)^2=h(p,p)I_4$ and $\beta\Gamma(p)^\dagger\beta=\Gamma(p)$ for every real $p$.
Multiplying $\Gamma(p)-\mu I_4$ and $\Gamma(p)+\mu I_4$ in either order gives $(h(p,p)-\mu^2)I_4$ by [step 1.1]. Thus $K(p)$ is invertible off shell and its inverse is exactly $S_0(p)$.
Since $\Gamma(p+k)-\Gamma(p)=\Gamma(k)$, the resolvent identity [F3] with $A=K(p)$, $B=K(p+k)$ gives $S_0(p+k)\Gamma(k)S_0(p)=S_0(p)-S_0(p+k)$.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Here
$\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ is the Schwartz space of smooth complex functions
whose coordinate-weighted derivatives are all bounded, as defined in
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]].
Fix an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space and an inertial coordinate
chart as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use coordinates
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ and metric $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, matching the
$(-+++)$ convention of the SR suppliers. Some QFT sources use its negative
$(+---)$; the Lorentz group is unchanged, and the phase is fixed explicitly
below.
Coordinates $x$ have length units, momenta have inverse-length units, and the
Fourier phase below is dimensionless. A parameter $\mu\ge0$ has inverse-length
units and is only a mathematical shell parameter; it is not identified with a
physical rest mass. For $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, set
$$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2},\qquad p_\mu(\mathbf k)=(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k).$$
The future mass shell is
$$H_\mu^+=\{(p^0,\mathbf p): (p^0)^2-|\mathbf p|^2=\mu^2,\ p^0>0\}.$$
When $\mu=0$, its apex is omitted; thus $\mathbf k\ne0$ in the massless
parameterization. The scalar shell pairing is
$$p\circ x:=p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$
Define the measure and one-particle Hilbert space by
$$d\nu_\mu(p_\mu(\mathbf k))= \frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)},\qquad H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C),$$
where the omitted massless apex has measure zero. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb
R^4)$ define its pointwise shell Fourier restriction by
$$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x.$$
The Fourier convention is exactly the displayed integral, with no prefactor.
If $\widehat f(\xi^0,\boldsymbol\xi)=
\int f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x^0\xi^0+\mathbf x\cdot\boldsymbol\xi)}\,d^4x$ denotes
the standard transform in
[[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]],
then
$$\mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p):=\int f(x)e^{i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)}\,d^4x =\widehat f\!\left(-\frac{p^0}{2\pi},\frac{\mathbf p}{2\pi}\right).$$
Its inverse is
$$f(x)=(2\pi)^{-4}\int_{\mathbb R^4} \mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p)e^{-i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)} \,dp^0\,d^3\mathbf p.$$
Thus this convention is a time reflection and rescaling of the cited
Schwartz automorphism and has the stated reciprocal normalization.
The proper orthochronous Lorentz group consists of linear maps preserving
$\eta$, orientation and the chosen future cone. A Poincare map is
$x\mapsto a+\Lambda x$ with $a\in\mathbb R^4$ and $\Lambda$ in that group.

This is a mathematical free scalar one-particle construction. It adopts the
chosen coordinates, measure and Fourier convention; it asserts no experimental
observation, physical mass identification or measurement outcome.

Order the generators as $\bar\psi_1,\ldots,\bar\psi_d,\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_d$. The corresponding ordered monomials form the $R$-basis of $\Lambda_d(R)$. Let
$$
M_d:=\bar\psi_1\cdots\bar\psi_d\psi_1\cdots\psi_d
$$
and let $[M_d]P\in R$ denote the coefficient of $M_d$ in $P\in\Lambda_d(R)$. Define the finite Grassmann integral by the $R$-linear functional
$$
\mathcal I_d(P):=(-1)^{d(d+1)/2}[M_d]P .
$$
For $K\in M_d(R)$, put $B_K:=\sum_{i,j=1}^d\bar\psi_iK_{ij}\psi_j$. Since every monomial of degree greater than $2d$ vanishes, its exponential is the finite sum
$$
\exp(-B_K):=\sum_{n=0}^{d}\frac{(-B_K)^n}{n!}.
$$
The sign factor in $\mathcal I_d$ is the chosen normalization. Its Gaussian determinant identity, including the value at $K=I_d$, is proved separately.

For a formal indeterminate $z$, let $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ be the commutative ring of sequences $(a_0,a_1,\ldots)$ written $\sum_{n\ge0}a_nz^n$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy-product multiplication. No convergence of a numerical series is part of this definition. For $d\ge1$, matrices over $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ use the usual finite matrix addition and multiplication.

Use the finite graph phase data of [[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]] and the QED $U(1)$, Clifford, and natural-unit conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Let $K_0(\zeta)\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$ be an invertible base matrix and let $V(\zeta)\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ be its finite link-hopping matrix. The admissible covariant families satisfy
$$ K_0(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta K_0(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad V(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta V(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1}. $$
The scalar base $K_0=mI_d$, $m\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, is an explicit admissible case. Define
$$ K(z;\zeta):=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta),\qquad S(z;\zeta):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-zK_0(\zeta)^{-1}V(\zeta))^nK_0(\zeta)^{-1}. $$
The coefficient of each power $z^n$ in $S$ is one finite matrix. The item defines this formal candidate; the following lemma proves its two-sided inverse and covariance properties. Define $\det A$ for a finite matrix $A$ over $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ by the Leibniz formula $\det A=\sum_{\sigma\in S_d}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{j=1}^d A_{j,\sigma(j)}$.

derivations.claim: Put $B_K=\sum_{i,j}\bar\psi_iK_{ij}\psi_j$. Every factor has Grassmann degree two, so a product of more than $d$ such factors has degree greater than $2d$ and vanishes. Hence the exponential is the finite sum $\sum_{n=0}^d(-B_K)^n/n!$, and only its degree-$2d$ term contributes to $[M_d]$.

In $B_K^d/d!$, any term with a repeated row or column index vanishes. The surviving terms are indexed by permutations $\sigma\in S_d$. Reordering $\bar\psi_1\psi_{\sigma(1)}\cdots\bar\psi_d\psi_{\sigma(d)}$ into $M_d$ contributes $(-1)^{d(d-1)/2}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$; the exponential contributes $(-1)^d$. Therefore
$$ [M_d]\exp(-B_K)=(-1)^{d(d+1)/2}\sum_{\sigma\in S_d}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i=1}^dK_{i,\sigma(i)} =(-1)^{d(d+1)/2}\det K . $$
Applying the normalization in [F1] proves the Gaussian identity.

For diagonal $D$, $K'_{ij}=u_iK_{ij}u_j^{-1}$. In each Leibniz term, $\prod_i u_i\prod_i u_{\sigma(i)}^{-1}=1$, since $\sigma$ permutes the indices; thus $\det K'=\det K$. The Gaussian identity from [step 2.1] then gives the same equality for the finite Grassmann integral.

For K=0 and d≥1 the exponential is 1 and its top coefficient and determinant vanish by step 2.1.
For d=1, I₁(1−barψ₁K₁₁ψ₁)=K₁₁, the one-by-one determinant in step 2.1.
No invertibility is assumed; singular K is covered by the permutation formula in steps 2.1 and 3.1.

These are conventions for constructed and formal calculations in this page pair. They are not empirical claims, physical postulates, or existence claims about an interacting continuum theory.

Use the geometric spacetime metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the time coordinate $x^0=ct$ in metres. For Clifford algebra and momentum contraction use the separate algebraic metric $h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$; a slash or a square of an energy four-vector uses $h$, never $\eta$.

A physical energy four-vector is $p=(E,c\mathbf p_{\rm phys})$, with each component in joules. Write $M=mc^2$ for rest energy in joules and $p^2=h(p,p)=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p_{\rm phys}|^2$. For two such vectors, $s=(p_1+p_2)^2$ is in $\mathrm J^2$. Natural momentum coordinates are the energy-vector components divided by $\hbar c$, in $\mathrm m^{-1}$; they are not substituted into SI formulas without restoring this factor. In the common natural-unit field convention, $\mu=mc/\hbar$ is in $\mathrm m^{-1}$, a scalar field has dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and a Dirac field has dimension $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$.

Take SI $e>0$ in coulombs, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, $c>0$ in metres per second, and $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Define
$$\alpha=\frac{e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0\hbar c},\qquad g=e\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0c}{\hbar}}=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha}>0.$$
Here $g$ is a dimensionless coupling. It is not the metric and not a gyromagnetic factor.

For gauge notation set $A_{\rm lower}=(-\phi/c,\mathbf A)$, with $A_a$ in tesla-metres and gauge function $\chi$ in webers. With charge $q$ in coulombs define
$$D_a=\partial_a-\frac{iqA_a}{\hbar},\qquad \psi\mapsto e^{iq\chi/\hbar}\psi,\qquad A\mapsto A+d\chi.$$
For the electron parameter use $q=-e$. The equivalent natural-unit coordinates are $A_{\rm nat}=A_{\rm SI}/\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}$ and $q_{\rm nat}=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$.

Finite-matrix examples act on $\mathbb C^d$ with the operator norm. For Hilbert spaces, use the first-variable-linear pairing $(u,v)_1=v^\dagger u$; a displayed coordinate contraction $u^\dagger v$ is second-variable-linear and equals $\overline{(u,v)_1}$. Thus norms, traces, and modulus-squared amplitudes agree under conversion, although the unsquared pairing is conjugated. No amplitude is assigned a probability by these conventions.

Use the finite Dirac matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], and the separate geometric metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and algebraic contraction $h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. Write $p=(E,\mathbf p)$ for an energy four-vector with components in joules, $M\geq0$ for a rest-energy parameter in joules, and $E=\sqrt{|\mathbf p|^2+M^2}>0$. In the natural-length variables of the Dirac definition, $\mathbf k=\mathbf p/(\hbar c)$, $\mu=M/(\hbar c)$, and $\omega=E/(\hbar c)$.

Let $\beta=\gamma^0$, $\alpha_j=\beta\gamma^j$, $\Sigma_j=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_j,\sigma_j)$, and $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$. Define $H_\pm=\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf p\pm\beta M$ and $P_\pm=(I_4+H_\pm/E)/2$. Each $P_\pm$ is a Hermitian rank-two projection. Choose orthonormal bases $\xi_{\pm,1},\xi_{\pm,2}$ of their ranges and put $u_s=\sqrt{2E}\xi_{+,s}$ and $v_s=\sqrt{2E}\xi_{-,s}$ for $s=1,2$. With $\bar z=z^\dagger\beta$ and $\not p=\gamma^0E-\sum_j\gamma^jp_j$, the following hold:

$$\operatorname{Tr}I_4=4,\quad \operatorname{Tr}\gamma^a=0,\quad \operatorname{Tr}(\gamma^a\gamma^b)=4h^{ab},\quad \operatorname{Tr}(\gamma^a\gamma^b\gamma^c)=0,$$

$$\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma^a\gamma^b\gamma^c\gamma^d) =4(h^{ab}h^{cd}-h^{ac}h^{bd}+h^{ad}h^{bc}), \qquad \sum_s u_s\bar u_s=\not p+M,\quad \sum_s v_s\bar v_s=\not p-M.$$

The columns satisfy $(\not p-M)u_s=0$ and $(\not p+M)v_s=0$. For all $x,y\in\mathbb C^4$, complex conjugation of a Dirac current is $\overline{\bar x\gamma^a y}=\bar y\gamma^a x$. The Countable Choice hypothesis written in the current draft [[def-qft-dirac-projections]] is retained as a supplier assumption; this finite-dimensional proof makes no additional choice use.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], and use [[def-qft-example-data]] and [[def-qft-example-two-body-phase-space-data]]. Write
$$\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M}=\{(E,\mathbf q)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3:E=\sqrt{|\mathbf q|^2+\mathsf M^2}\}$$
for the positive shell in that Definition, and $C_+=\{(E,\mathbf q)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3:E\geq|\mathbf q|\}$ for the closed future cone of $h=(+,-,-,-)$. A proper orthochronous linear $h$-Lorentz map is a real linear $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda^Th\Lambda=h$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and $\Lambda(C_+)=C_+$. For energy four-vectors on these positive shells, the shell measure $d^3\mathbf p/((2\pi)^3\,2E)$ is invariant under every such map. Let $\mathsf M_1,\mathsf M_2\geq0$, let $P$ be future timelike, meaning $P^0>0$ and $h(P,P)>0$, set $s=h(P,P)>(\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2)^2$, and write $E_i(r)=\sqrt{r^2+\mathsf M_i^2}$. Let $f$ be a nonnegative Borel function on $\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M_1}\times\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M_2}$. For a proper orthochronous $h$-Lorentz map $\Lambda_P$ with $\Lambda_P P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$, define the finite Borel measure $\Phi_{2,P}$ as the pushforward of $\frac{k_*}{16\pi^2\sqrt{s}}d\Omega$ under

is interpreted by first evaluating the spatial delta in $k_2$, then the one-dimensional energy delta by the increasing radial change of variable $r\mapsto E_1(r)+E_2(r)$. It equals $\int f\,d\Phi_{2,P}$. The threshold root is $k_*$ in that Definition, and
$$\int d\Phi_{2,P}=\int d\Phi_2=\frac{k_*}{4\pi\sqrt{s}}.$$
For equal rest energies $\mathsf M_1=\mathsf M_2=\mathsf M$, set $\beta=\sqrt{1-4\mathsf M^2/s}$; then $k_*=\sqrt{s}\beta/2$ and $\int d\Phi_{2,P}=\int d\Phi_2=\beta/(8\pi)$. For the scattering flux identities, take incoming $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)\in\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M_{i,\mathrm{in}}}$, where $\mathsf M_{i,\mathrm{in}}\geq0$, and require $p_1+p_2=P$. A center-of-momentum map is a proper orthochronous $h$-Lorentz map $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$; write $\Lambda p_1=(E_1^*,\mathbf p_1^*)$ and define $p_*=|\mathbf p_1^*|$. The value is independent of the choice of $\Lambda$, since two such maps differ by a spatial rotation. Their invariant flux is $F=4p_*\sqrt{s}$. For equal incoming rest energies $\mathsf M_{\mathrm{in}}\geq0$ with $s\geq4\mathsf M_{\mathrm{in}}^2$, define $\beta_{\mathrm{in}}=\sqrt{1-4\mathsf M_{\mathrm{in}}^2/s}$; then $p_*=\sqrt{s}\beta_{\mathrm{in}}/2$ and $F=2s\beta_{\mathrm{in}}$. For finite nonempty incoming and outgoing label sets, normalized initial weights, and the Borel amplitude family of the Definition, whenever $F>0$ the cross-section coefficient map gives
$$\frac{d\sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}}{d\Omega} =\frac{(\hbar c)^2}{64\pi^2s}\, \frac{k_*}{p_*}\, \frac{\overline{|\mathcal A|^2}}{S_f}.$$
For a parent at rest, represented by $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$ with $\mathsf M_0>2\mathsf M$, and two equal-rest-energy daughters on $\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M}$ with total four-vector $P_0$ and constant amplitude $G_E$ in joules, the rate coefficient is $|G_E|^2\sqrt{1-4\mathsf M^2/\mathsf M_0^2}/(32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0)$ when the daughters are identical. This is a coefficient calculation, not a claim of exponential survival.

Let $K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)$ and $S(z;\zeta)$ be the finite-dimensional formal matrices of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]], with $d\ge1$, $K_0(\zeta)$ invertible, and both coefficient matrices covariant under the vertex phase angles of [[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Then $S$ is a two-sided inverse of $K$ in $M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$, and
$$ S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1} $$
coefficientwise. For a real vertex tuple $\theta$, put
$\Theta:=\operatorname{diag}_{x\in X}(\theta_xI_r)$,
$\zeta_s:=\zeta^{s\theta}$, and $D_s:=D_{s\theta}=e^{is\Theta}$.
Write $K_s:=K(z;\zeta_s)$ and $S_s:=S(z;\zeta_s)$, and define
$\delta K:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}K_s\right|_{s=0}$ and
$\delta S:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}S_s\right|_{s=0}$ coefficientwise along this
differentiable phase path. The variations satisfy
$$ \delta K=i[\Theta,K],\qquad \delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S . $$
For ordinary finite matrices $A,B\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$, the corresponding resolvent identity is $B^{-1}(B-A)A^{-1}=A^{-1}-B^{-1}$. These are formal or finite algebraic statements; they assert no convergence of a perturbation series, continuum limit, or loop Ward identity.

By [F2], the spin sums reduce the squared-current factors to
$$L_e^{ab}=\frac14\operatorname{Tr}[(\not p_2-m)\gamma^a(\not p_1+m)\gamma^b], \qquad L_{\mu,ab}=\operatorname{Tr}[(\not k_1+M)\gamma_a(\not k_2-M)\gamma_b].$$
The odd traces vanish. Expanding the even terms with [F2] and using $p_1\cdot p_2+m^2=s/2$ and $k_1\cdot k_2+M^2=s/2$ gives
$$L_e^{ab}=p_2^ap_1^b+p_2^bp_1^a-\frac{s}{2}h^{ab}, \qquad L_{\mu,ab}=4(k_{1a}k_{2b}+k_{1b}k_{2a}-\frac{s}{2}h_{ab}).$$
These mass-shell dot products follow from $(p_1+p_2)^2=(k_1+k_2)^2=s$.

Contracting the tensors gives
$$L_e^{ab}L_{\mu,ab} =4\{2[(p_2\cdot k_1)(p_1\cdot k_2)+(p_2\cdot k_2)(p_1\cdot k_1)] +s^2-s(p_1\cdot p_2+k_1\cdot k_2)\}.$$
The two cross-metric terms contribute $-s(p_1\cdot p_2+k_1\cdot k_2)$, while the metric-metric term contributes $s^2$; substituting $p_1\cdot p_2=(s-2m^2)/2$ and $k_1\cdot k_2=(s-2M^2)/2$ reduces the last two terms to $s(m^2+M^2)$.

The finite matrix hypothesis [L1] supplies coefficientwise inverse and phase-covariance identities only for its specified finite graph kernel. For the separate amplitude in [A1], the spinor equations from [F2] give $ ar v(p_2)
ot p_2=-m ar v(p_2)$ and $
ot p_1u(p_1)=mu(p_1)$, so their sum contracted with the incoming current is zero. Likewise $ ar u(k_1)
ot k_1=M ar u(k_1)$ and $
ot k_2v(k_2)=-Mv(k_2)$, so the outgoing current is transverse to $P=k_1+k_2$. A longitudinal propagator term is therefore multiplied by two zero contractions. No broader tree-current claim is taken from [L1].

In the center-of-momentum frame take $|\mathbf p_1|=\sqrt{s}\beta_e/2$, $|\mathbf k_1|=\sqrt{s}\beta_\mu/2$, and let $\theta$ be the angle between them. The four cross-dot-products in step 2.1 are $s/4\pm|\mathbf p_1||\mathbf k_1|\cos\theta$, with each sign occurring twice. Substitution into step 2.1 and multiplication by $g^4/s^2$ gives $\overline{|\mathcal M|^2}=g^4[3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta]$. The resulting function of $\theta$ is continuous and therefore Borel; the spin-label sums are finite by [F2]. The strict threshold gives positive $\beta_e,\beta_\mu$, and [F3] gives incoming flux $F=2s\beta_e>0$.

For distinguishable final particles, [F3] gives $d\Phi_2/d\Omega=\beta_\mu/(32\pi^2)$ and $F=2s\beta_e$. Substituting the squared amplitude from step 3.1 into [F3] yields the displayed differential coefficient after using $g^4=(4\pi\alpha)^2$. Integrating uses $\int_{S^2}d\Omega=4\pi$ and $\int_{S^2}\cos^2\theta\,d\Omega=4\pi/3$, giving the displayed total coefficient.

For $\delta=4m^2/s\leq1/2$, set $B_0=2-\beta_\mu^2+\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta$ and $Q=1-\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta$. Then $B_0\geq1$, $0\leq Q\leq1$, and the ratio of the full coefficient to its $m=0$ value is $R=(B_0+\delta Q)/(B_0\sqrt{1-\delta})\geq1$. Also
$$R-1=\frac1{\sqrt{1-\delta}}-1+ \frac{\delta Q}{B_0\sqrt{1-\delta}} \leq2\sqrt2\,\delta\leq4\delta,$$
because $1/\sqrt{1-\delta}-1\leq\sqrt2\,\delta$ and $B_0\sqrt{1-\delta}\geq1/\sqrt2$. This compares only the two formal tree coefficients.

For the **exact finite-regulator class** used on this page, the state space is

an evaluated function, exact probability, convergent perturbation series, or
error bound. A formal coefficient can be assigned a phenomenological meaning
only by a separate, model-specific physical adoption with its approximation
scope stated.

finite record of measurement outcomes under the stated preparation, apparatus,
calibration, sampling, and analysis conditions. Its reported uncertainty and
conditions travel with the estimate. It is not the exact model value, and it
does not prove the framework used to interpret it. The 2022 Fan et al. report
is an example of a source-reported electron magnetic-moment determination;
this definition supplies no numerical result, uncertainty reconstruction, or
new experimental claim.

Primitive and derived status is formulation-relative. In a selected regulated
model, the regulator, Hamiltonian data, coupling, initial state, and supplied
measurement are declared inputs; an evolution, amplitude, or probability law
is derived only when the construction and adopted rule establish it. In a
formal calculation, the specified masses, couplings, coefficient rules, and
subtraction prescription are inputs, while its listed coefficients are
derived within that formal calculation. An empirical estimate is a reported
data-analysis result, not a primitive model parameter or a theorem.

The following units are examples of types, not identifications of quantities:
a cross section $\sigma$ is area-valued with SI unit $\mathrm{m^2}$; a rate
$\Gamma$ is inverse-time-valued with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; an energy width
$\Gamma_E$ has unit joule. Only a separately stated convention may identify
$\Gamma_E=\hbar\Gamma$. The fine-structure parameter $\alpha$, a dimensionless
coupling $g$, and a gyromagnetic factor $g_s$ are dimensionless but have
different physical meanings. The name “width,” a common symbol, or matching
dimensions does not supply an exponential-decay law or an equality between
these parameters.

Use the finite Dirac matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], and the separate geometric metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and algebraic contraction $h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. Write $p=(E,\mathbf p)$ for an energy four-vector with components in joules, $M\geq0$ for a rest-energy parameter in joules, and $E=\sqrt{|\mathbf p|^2+M^2}>0$. In the natural-length variables of the Dirac definition, $\mathbf k=\mathbf p/(\hbar c)$, $\mu=M/(\hbar c)$, and $\omega=E/(\hbar c)$.

Let $\beta=\gamma^0$, $\alpha_j=\beta\gamma^j$, $\Sigma_j=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_j,\sigma_j)$, and $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$. Define $H_\pm=\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf p\pm\beta M$ and $P_\pm=(I_4+H_\pm/E)/2$. Each $P_\pm$ is a Hermitian rank-two projection. Choose orthonormal bases $\xi_{\pm,1},\xi_{\pm,2}$ of their ranges and put $u_s=\sqrt{2E}\xi_{+,s}$ and $v_s=\sqrt{2E}\xi_{-,s}$ for $s=1,2$. With $\bar z=z^\dagger\beta$ and $\not p=\gamma^0E-\sum_j\gamma^jp_j$, the following hold:

$$\operatorname{Tr}I_4=4,\quad \operatorname{Tr}\gamma^a=0,\quad \operatorname{Tr}(\gamma^a\gamma^b)=4h^{ab},\quad \operatorname{Tr}(\gamma^a\gamma^b\gamma^c)=0,$$

$$\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma^a\gamma^b\gamma^c\gamma^d) =4(h^{ab}h^{cd}-h^{ac}h^{bd}+h^{ad}h^{bc}), \qquad \sum_s u_s\bar u_s=\not p+M,\quad \sum_s v_s\bar v_s=\not p-M.$$

The columns satisfy $(\not p-M)u_s=0$ and $(\not p+M)v_s=0$. For all $x,y\in\mathbb C^4$, complex conjugation of a Dirac current is $\overline{\bar x\gamma^a y}=\bar y\gamma^a x$. The Countable Choice hypothesis written in the current draft [[def-qft-dirac-projections]] is retained as a supplier assumption; this finite-dimensional proof makes no additional choice use.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], and use [[def-qft-example-data]] and [[def-qft-example-two-body-phase-space-data]]. Write
$$\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M}=\{(E,\mathbf q)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3:E=\sqrt{|\mathbf q|^2+\mathsf M^2}\}$$
for the positive shell in that Definition, and $C_+=\{(E,\mathbf q)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3:E\geq|\mathbf q|\}$ for the closed future cone of $h=(+,-,-,-)$. A proper orthochronous linear $h$-Lorentz map is a real linear $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda^Th\Lambda=h$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and $\Lambda(C_+)=C_+$. For energy four-vectors on these positive shells, the shell measure $d^3\mathbf p/((2\pi)^3\,2E)$ is invariant under every such map. Let $\mathsf M_1,\mathsf M_2\geq0$, let $P$ be future timelike, meaning $P^0>0$ and $h(P,P)>0$, set $s=h(P,P)>(\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2)^2$, and write $E_i(r)=\sqrt{r^2+\mathsf M_i^2}$. Let $f$ be a nonnegative Borel function on $\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M_1}\times\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M_2}$. For a proper orthochronous $h$-Lorentz map $\Lambda_P$ with $\Lambda_P P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$, define the finite Borel measure $\Phi_{2,P}$ as the pushforward of $\frac{k_*}{16\pi^2\sqrt{s}}d\Omega$ under
$$\mathbf n\longmapsto\left(\Lambda_P^{-1}(E_1^*,k_*\mathbf n),\Lambda_P^{-1}(E_2^*,-k_*\mathbf n)\right),$$
where $E_i^*$ and $k_*$ are from [[def-qft-example-two-body-phase-space-data]]. The proof below shows that $\Phi_{2,P}$ is independent of the choice of $\Lambda_P$; for $P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ it is exactly the center-of-momentum measure $d\Phi_2$ in that Definition. The standard two-body on-shell integral
$$(2\pi)^4\int d\nu_{\mathsf M_1}(k_1)d\nu_{\mathsf M_2}(k_2)\, \delta^{(4)}(P-k_1-k_2)\,f(k_1,k_2)$$
is interpreted by first evaluating the spatial delta in $k_2$, then the one-dimensional energy delta by the increasing radial change of variable $r\mapsto E_1(r)+E_2(r)$. Explicitly, for each fixed angular direction and nonnegative Borel radial function $g:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty]$, the radial action after spatial evaluation is $\int_0^\infty g(r)\delta(\sqrt{s}-E_1(r)-E_2(r))\,dr=g(k_*)/(d(E_1+E_2)/dr|_{k_*})$; this is the pushforward evaluation under that $C^1$ diffeomorphism, not a product of distributions. It equals $\int f\,d\Phi_{2,P}$. The threshold root is $k_*$ in that Definition, and
$$\int d\Phi_{2,P}=\int d\Phi_2=\frac{k_*}{4\pi\sqrt{s}}.$$
For equal rest energies $\mathsf M_1=\mathsf M_2=\mathsf M$, set $\beta=\sqrt{1-4\mathsf M^2/s}$; then $k_*=\sqrt{s}\beta/2$ and $\int d\Phi_{2,P}=\int d\Phi_2=\beta/(8\pi)$. For the scattering flux identities, take incoming $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)\in\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M_{i,\mathrm{in}}}$, where $\mathsf M_{i,\mathrm{in}}\geq0$, and require $p_1+p_2=P$. A center-of-momentum map is a proper orthochronous $h$-Lorentz map $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$; write $\Lambda p_1=(E_1^*,\mathbf p_1^*)$ and define $p_*=|\mathbf p_1^*|$. The value is independent of the choice of $\Lambda$, since two such maps differ by a spatial rotation. Their invariant flux is $F=4p_*\sqrt{s}$. For equal incoming rest energies $\mathsf M_{\mathrm{in}}\geq0$ with $s\geq4\mathsf M_{\mathrm{in}}^2$, define $\beta_{\mathrm{in}}=\sqrt{1-4\mathsf M_{\mathrm{in}}^2/s}$; then $p_*=\sqrt{s}\beta_{\mathrm{in}}/2$ and $F=2s\beta_{\mathrm{in}}$. For finite nonempty incoming and outgoing label sets, normalized initial weights, and the Borel amplitude family of the Definition, whenever $F>0$ the cross-section coefficient map gives
$$\frac{d\sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}}{d\Omega} =\frac{(\hbar c)^2}{64\pi^2s}\, \frac{k_*}{p_*}\, \frac{\overline{|\mathcal A|^2}}{S_f}.$$
For a parent at rest, represented by $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$ with $\mathsf M_0>2\mathsf M$, and two equal-rest-energy daughters on $\mathcal H^+_{\mathsf M}$ with total four-vector $P_0$ and constant amplitude $G_E$ in joules, the rate coefficient is $|G_E|^2\sqrt{1-4\mathsf M^2/\mathsf M_0^2}/(32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0)$ when the daughters are identical. This is a coefficient calculation, not a claim of exponential survival.

Let $m\geq0$ be a scalar rest energy in joules, and let $p_1,p_2,k_1,k_2$ be the incoming and outgoing scattering vectors on the positive $m$-shell of [[def-qft-example-two-body-phase-space-data]], so each $(E,\mathbf q)$ satisfies $E=\sqrt{|\mathbf q|^2+m^2}>0$. Require $p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and $s=h(P,P)>4m^2$, with $h$ as in [[def-qft-example-data]]. Evaluate the coefficient map in a center-of-momentum frame $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as defined in [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. For one scalar initial label of weight $1$ and one specified final channel, take the dimensionless real quartic tree amplitude $\mathcal A=-\lambda$. The coefficient map of [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]] gives
$$\frac{d\sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}}{d\Omega} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{128\pi^2s}, \qquad \sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}=\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s}$$
for identical final scalars integrated over the full labeled sphere. For distinguishable final scalars the two coefficients are twice these values.

For a parent at rest, $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$ with energy $\mathsf M_0>2m$, decaying through a specified single channel to two identical scalars on the positive $m$-shell whose total four-vector is $P_0$, under a constant amplitude $G_E$ in joules, the rate coefficient is
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{coeff}} =\frac{|G_E|^2}{32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0} \sqrt{1-\frac{4m^2}{\mathsf M_0^2}}.$$
This result concerns the defined formal coefficients. It does not assert an exact exponential survival law.

For a specifically named finite tree calculation, adopt its selected formal
diagram coefficient as a **leading perturbative coefficient** with a stated
phenomenological reading. For QED, use the vertex and free-line conventions
of the current draft supplier
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]]. A particle of natural charge $q_n$ has
vertex $iq_n\gamma^a$; the electron has $q_n=-e_n$ and vertex
$-ie_n\gamma^a$. The rational fermion line is
$$ i\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}, $$
for $\mu>0$ and off-shell $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$. In Feynman gauge
the auxiliary photon line is
$$ -i\frac{h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}=i\frac{\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}. $$

[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]] is part of the formal convention and
asserts no convergence. If a time-ordered distribution is used, use the
actual free carrier specified there; that identification is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]. The displayed pole notation does not define loop
products. In the pair-production channel below the selected muon also has
model charge $-e$, and only the photon line is internal.

labels, and a specified formal amplitude $\mathcal A$, adopt the
cross-section coefficient map of
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. Its scattering inputs are
positive-shell energy vectors $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)$ with
$E_i=\sqrt{|\mathbf p_i|^2+\mathsf M_{i,\rm in}^2}>0$,

shells. Require $s=h(P,P)>(\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2)^2$ for the outgoing
rest energies and positive incoming flux $F>0$, precisely the supplier's
admissible scattering domain. In the center-of-momentum frame it
uses the invariant incoming flux $F$, the two-body measure $d\Phi_2$, and the
final-state factor $S_f=2$ for identical particles or $S_f=1$ for
distinguishable particles, integrated over the full labeled sphere. When
this coefficient is read phenomenologically, the initial preparation,
channel, threshold, and approximation are part of the model statement. No
universal error estimate for omitted terms is implied.

For the scalar examples, separately adopt the constant formal amplitudes
$\mathcal A=-\lambda$ for the quartic contact channel and $\mathcal G=G_E$
for the cubic parent decay, with the units and external normalization stated
at each use. The scalar scattering inputs lie on their stated positive
shells with a common total and the same strict threshold and positive-flux
conditions. For decay, the parent is $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$,
$\mathsf M_0>\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2$, and its two positive-shell daughters
sum to $P_0$. Their coefficient map is the one in
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. If a rate $\Gamma$ is reported as
an energy width, the convention is explicitly $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma$; it
does not supply a survival law.

The readings above do not identify a formal coefficient with an exact
continuum cross section, probability, decay rate, or measured estimate. In
particular they do not construct an interacting continuum $S$-matrix or LSZ
limit, establish convergence of a perturbation series, bound loop or
soft-radiation effects, specify beam or detector cuts, resolve threshold
resummation, or reproduce the statistical analysis of an experiment. A
comparison with observations would require the actual apparatus, sampling,
calibration, uncertainty, and radiative-inclusiveness conditions. The
reported electron magnetic-moment measurements, including the Fan et al.
report listed in the source references, remain source-reported
empirical results and are not premises of this adoption.

Adopt the following coefficient convention for finite formal QED bookkeeping in
the Minkowski, units, and Clifford conventions of
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. In particular,
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $h=-\eta$,
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=2h^{ab}I_4$, and
$\not p:=\gamma^a h_{ab}p^b$. The inverse-length mass is
$\mu=m_{\rm rest,SI}c/\hbar$ and a declared physical charge $q_{\rm SI}$ has
dimensionless value $q_{\rm n}=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$.

A **formal coefficient graph** here is a finite directed graph of interaction
vertices and internal lines with a momentum covector assigned to each line and
momentum conservation imposed at each vertex. It records a coefficient at a
fixed finite or formal order; it is not, by this definition, a convergent
amplitude or an operator on a continuum interacting Hilbert space. For a Dirac
species of dimensionless charge $g$, use $D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a$ and adopt the
vertex factor $ig\gamma^a$. For an electron, $g=-e_{\rm n}$, so the vertex is
$-ie_{\rm n}\gamma^a$.

For $\mu>0$ and off-shell momentum $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$, set
$$S_0(p)=\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}.$$
The adopted fermion-line coefficient is $iS_0(p)$. In Feynman gauge the
auxiliary covariant photon-line coefficient is
$$D^F_{ab}(k)=-\frac{i h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}
=\frac{i\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}.$$
The symbol $+i0$ denotes the selected Feynman boundary-value convention when a
distributional line is used; it does not define products of singular loop
distributions. The coefficient $D^F_{ab}$ is a calculational tensor factor,
not a declaration of four positive physical photon polarization states.

For the formal matrix realization, use the coefficientwise inverse specified
by the planned interface [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]: if $K_0$ is an invertible
finite matrix and $K(z)=K_0+zV$, the formal inverse is the power series in
$z$; no convergence in $z$ is claimed. The planned off-shell/tree identities
of [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]] fix the $h=-\eta$ slash and the nonzero-denominator
conditions. When a time-ordered free distribution is needed, use the actual
carrier $H_\mu$ of [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]], for which
$(\Box-\mu^2)H_\mu=i\delta_0$ and whose definition has no extra prefactor
$i$. The distributional use of that carrier is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]; the formal coefficient factors above are adopted
independently of that optional distributional identification.

derivations.claim: In the center-of-momentum frame the selected photon momentum is $P$ and $h(P,P)=s>0$. The current QFT-G02 convention [A3] supplies two charge-$-e_n$ vertices and photon factor $-ih_{ab}/(s+i0)$. At this regular point, $\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}(s+i\epsilon)^{-1}=s^{-1}$, so the scalar denominator is $1/s$. Under the selected-graph normalization [A2], the remaining spin dependence is the stated product of the two currents, up to a common phase that vanishes from the modulus square. This calculation uses no internal fermion line or loop product.

Summing the final spin labels and averaging the four initial pairs, [F3] reduces the squared currents to $$ L_e^{ab}= rac14\operatorname{Tr}[(
ot p_2-m)\gamma^a(
ot p_1+m)\gamma^b],\qquad L_{\mu,ab}=\operatorname{Tr}[(
ot k_1+M)\gamma_a(
ot k_2-M)\gamma_b]. $$ The terms with three gamma matrices vanish. Expanding the remaining terms with the two- and four-gamma traces in [F3] gives $$ L_e^{ab}=p_2^ap_1^b+p_2^bp_1^a- rac{s}{2}h^{ab},\qquad L_{\mu,ab}=4(k_{1a}k_{2b}+k_{1b}k_{2a}- rac{s}{2}h_{ab}), $$ because $p_1\cdot p_2+m^2=s/2$ and $k_1\cdot k_2+M^2=s/2$ follow by expanding the two total-momentum squares.

The adjoint equations from [F3] give $ ar v(p_2)
ot p_2=-m ar v(p_2)$ and $
ot p_1u(p_1)=mu(p_1)$, so contraction with $P=p_1+p_2$ cancels the two terms. Similarly, $ ar u(k_1)
ot k_1=M ar u(k_1)$ and $
ot k_2v(k_2)=-Mv(k_2)$ cancel in the outgoing current. This proves both displayed current contractions, including when either mass is zero; no general off-shell or loop Ward statement is inferred.

The declared positive-shell scalar inputs, common total and center-of-momentum evaluation meet [F5] exactly; the decay daughters have total $P_0$ and satisfy its strict rest-parent threshold. Apply [F5] to these declared scalar amplitudes and thresholds. Its identical-final factor is $S_f=2$ on the full labeled sphere, while the distinguishable case has $S_f=1$, so the total scattering coefficients have the stated factor of two. The decay result uses the same identical-particle factor and the parent-rest coefficient map. Since $[G_E]=[m_s]=[\mathsf M_0]=\mathrm J$ and $[\hbar]=\mathrm{J\,s}$, $[\Gamma_{\rm coeff}]=\mathrm J^2/(\mathrm{J\,s\,J})=\mathrm{s}^{-1}$; $(\hbar c)^2/s$ has unit $\mathrm{m}^2$.

In this chart $P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ gives $\mathbf p_2=-\mathbf p_1$ and $E_1+E_2=\sqrt{s}$. The equal mass-shell equations and $E_i>0$ imply $E_1=E_2=\sqrt{s}/2$, hence $|\mathbf p_1|=\sqrt{s/4-m^2}=\sqrt{s}\beta_e/2>0$; the same argument gives $\widetilde E_1=\widetilde E_2=\sqrt{s}/2$ and $|\mathbf k_1|=\sqrt{s}\beta_\mu/2>0$. Thus $\theta$ is defined. If $\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2$ both send $P$ to rest, $\Lambda_2\Lambda_1^{-1}$ fixes $(1,\mathbf0)$ and so acts by a proper spatial rotation by [F4]; it preserves the Euclidean dot product, making $\theta$ independent of the selected chart's residual orientation. Contracting the tensors in 1.2 and using the mass-shell dot products gives $$ L_e^{ab}L_{\mu,ab}=4\{2[(p_2\cdot k_1)(p_1\cdot k_2)+(p_2\cdot k_2)(p_1\cdot k_1)] +s^2-s(p_1\cdot p_2+k_1\cdot k_2)\}. $$ The cross terms with one metric contribute $-s(p_1\cdot p_2+k_1\cdot k_2)$, and the metric-metric term contributes $s^2$; together these equal $s(m^2+M^2)$. The mixed dot products are $p_2\cdot k_1=p_1\cdot k_2=s/4+|\mathbf p_1||\mathbf k_1|\cos\theta$ and $p_2\cdot k_2=p_1\cdot k_1=s/4-|\mathbf p_1||\mathbf k_1|\cos\theta$. Substituting and multiplying by $g^4/s^2$ gives the stated spin-averaged squared coefficient.

The strict threshold gives $\beta_e,\beta_\mu>0$. For distinguishable muon labels, [F4] gives $d\Phi_2/d\Omega=\beta_\mu/(32\pi^2)$ and $F=2s\beta_e$. Inserting the squared coefficient derived in step 2.1 into its map and using $g^4=(4\pi\alpha)^2$ yields the displayed differential coefficient. The sphere integrals are $\int d\Omega=4\pi$ and $\int\cos^2\theta\,d\Omega=4\pi/3$ (integrate $2\pi u^2$ over $-1\leq u\leq1$), giving the displayed total coefficient.

If $\delta=4m^2/s\leq1/2$, set $$ B_0=2-\beta_\mu^2+\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta,\qquad Q=1-\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta. $$ Then $B_0\geq1$ and $0\leq Q\leq1$. The ratio of the full differential coefficient to its $m=0$ value is $$ R=\frac{B_0+\delta Q}{B_0\sqrt{1-\delta}}\geq1. $$ Moreover $$ R-1=\frac1{\sqrt{1-\delta}}-1+ \frac{\delta Q}{B_0\sqrt{1-\delta}} \leq2\sqrt2\,\delta\leq4\delta, $$ since $1/\sqrt{1-\delta}-1\leq\sqrt2\delta$ and $B_0\sqrt{1-\delta}\geq1/\sqrt2$. This compares only the two formal tree coefficients.

The units and formal/empirical types in [F1]–[F2] identify the results as formal coefficients with area or inverse-time units. The adopted interpretation in [A1] gives only the named leading-coefficient reading; neither an exact continuum observable, a measured estimate, nor an exponential survival law follows.

Adopt the following coefficient convention for finite formal QED bookkeeping in
the Minkowski, units, and Clifford conventions of
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. In particular,
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $h=-\eta$,
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=2h^{ab}I_4$, and
$\not p:=\gamma^a h_{ab}p^b$. The inverse-length mass is
$\mu=m_{\rm rest,SI}c/\hbar$ and a declared physical charge $q_{\rm SI}$ has
dimensionless value $q_{\rm n}=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$.

A **formal coefficient graph** here is a finite directed graph of interaction
vertices and internal lines with a momentum covector assigned to each line and
momentum conservation imposed at each vertex. It records a coefficient at a
fixed finite or formal order; it is not, by this definition, a convergent
amplitude or an operator on a continuum interacting Hilbert space. For a Dirac
species of dimensionless charge $g$, use $D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a$ and adopt the
vertex factor $ig\gamma^a$. For an electron, $g=-e_{\rm n}$, so the vertex is
$-ie_{\rm n}\gamma^a$.

For $\mu>0$ and off-shell momentum $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$, set
$$S_0(p)=\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}.$$
The adopted fermion-line coefficient is $iS_0(p)$. In Feynman gauge the
auxiliary covariant photon-line coefficient is
$$D^F_{ab}(k)=-\frac{i h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}
=\frac{i\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}.$$
The symbol $+i0$ denotes the selected Feynman boundary-value convention when a
distributional line is used; it does not define products of singular loop
distributions. The coefficient $D^F_{ab}$ is a calculational tensor factor,
not a declaration of four positive physical photon polarization states.

For the formal matrix realization, use the coefficientwise inverse specified
by the planned interface [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]: if $K_0$ is an invertible
finite matrix and $K(z)=K_0+zV$, the formal inverse is the power series in
$z$; no convergence in $z$ is claimed. The planned off-shell/tree identities
of [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]] fix the $h=-\eta$ slash and the nonzero-denominator
conditions. When a time-ordered free distribution is needed, use the actual
carrier $H_\mu$ of [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]], for which
$(\Box-\mu^2)H_\mu=i\delta_0$ and whose definition has no extra prefactor
$i$. The distributional use of that carrier is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]; the formal coefficient factors above are adopted
independently of that optional distributional identification.

products. In the pair-production channel below the selected muon also has
model charge $-e$, and only the photon line is internal.

For declared incoming spin probabilities, sum over declared final spin
labels, and a specified formal amplitude $\mathcal A$, adopt the
cross-section coefficient map of
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. In the center-of-momentum frame it
uses the invariant incoming flux $F$, the two-body measure $d\Phi_2$, and the
final-state factor $S_f=2$ for identical particles or $S_f=1$ for
distinguishable particles, integrated over the full labeled sphere. When
this coefficient is read phenomenologically, the initial preparation,
channel, threshold, and approximation are part of the model statement. No

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the fixed Cartesian
Minkowski chart $x=(ct,\mathbf x)$, the geometric metric
$\eta=(-,+,+,+)$, and the distinct algebraic contraction
$h=-\eta=(+,-,-,-)$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. Let $m,M\geq0$ be the
electron and muon rest energies in joules. In this chart, a future energy
four-vector is
$q=(E,\mathbf q)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $E>0$; it has rest energy $\mathsf M\geq0$
when $h(q,q)=\mathsf M^2$. All four-vector components are in joules, and
$\mathbf q$ is $c$ times physical spatial momentum. Let $p_1,p_2$ be future electron
and positron energy four-vectors with rest energy $m$, and $k_1,k_2$ future
muon and antimuon energy four-vectors with rest energy $M$, satisfying
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and
$$ s=h(P,P)>4\max(m^2,M^2). $$
By [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]], choose a proper orthochronous
$h$-Lorentz matrix $\Lambda\in GL(4,\mathbb R)$, meaning
$\Lambda^Th\Lambda=h$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and preservation of the future
causal cone $C_+:=\{(E,\mathbf q):E>0,\ h((E,\mathbf q),(E,\mathbf q))\geq0\}$,
with $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$.
Its boost construction supplies such a map because $P$ is future timelike.
The **center-of-momentum inertial chart** has coordinates
$x^{\rm CM}=\Lambda x$ on spacetime and corresponding four-vector components
$q^{\rm CM}=\Lambda q$; from here on, four-vector components are in that
chart, so $P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$. The strict threshold makes
$\mathbf p_1$ and $\mathbf k_1$ nonzero. Define the
scattering angle $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ by
$$\theta:=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\mathbf p_1\cdot\mathbf k_1}{|\mathbf p_1|\,|\mathbf k_1|}\right),$$
using the Euclidean inner product on $\mathbb R^3$.
Write $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha}>0$, as in
[[def-qft-example-data]], and
$$ \beta_e=\sqrt{1-\frac{4m^2}{s}},\qquad \beta_\mu=\sqrt{1-\frac{4M^2}{s}}. $$
For the selected formal one-photon tree coefficient, take equal incoherent
weight $1/4$ for the four initial spin-label pairs and sum over final spin
labels. Take the selected muon model charge to be $-e$ as well. Up to an
irrelevant common phase, its amplitude is
$$ \mathcal M_{\rm tree}=\frac{g^2}{s} [\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)] [\bar u(k_1)\gamma_a v(k_2)], $$
where the brackets denote the product of the two currents. This selected
formal amplitude adopts the current draft QFT-G02 line/vertex convention;
it is not an exact amplitude of a constructed continuum theory.

Conditional on this amplitude adoption and
[[post-qft-example-formal-observable-map]], the spin-averaged squared
coefficient is
$$ \overline{|\mathcal M_{\rm tree}|^2} =g^4[3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2 +\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta], $$
The distinguishable-particle differential and total
cross-section coefficients are
$$ \frac{d\sigma_{\rm coeff}}{d\Omega} =\frac{\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2\beta_\mu}{4s\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta], $$
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff} =\frac{\pi\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{s}\frac{\beta_\mu}{\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\tfrac13\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2]. $$
For $\delta=4m^2/s\leq1/2$, the ratio of this differential coefficient to
the coefficient at $m=0$ with the same $M,s,\theta$ belongs to
$[1,1+4\delta]$. This bound is only the incoming-electron-mass effect
within the selected tree coefficient.

The on-shell equations also give
$$ P_a\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)=0,\qquad P_a\bar u(k_1)\gamma^a v(k_2)=0. $$
These are the two current contractions for this finite external-spinor
calculation; they do not assert an all-orders or loop Ward theorem.

For the separate scalar conventions of
[[post-qft-example-formal-observable-map]], let $m_s\geq0$ be a scalar rest
energy, let the incoming $r_1,r_2$ and outgoing $l_1,l_2$ lie on the
positive $m_s$-shell, meaning each $(E,\mathbf q)$ has
$E=\sqrt{|\mathbf q|^2+m_s^2}>0$, and require
$r_1+r_2=l_1+l_2=P_s$ with $s=h(P_s,P_s)>4m_s^2$.
Evaluate in a proper orthochronous center-of-momentum chart taking $P_s$
to $(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as in [F4]. Let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ be the dimensionless
constant quartic amplitude parameter. The identical-final full-sphere and
distinguishable total coefficients are respectively
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm identical} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s},\qquad \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm distinguishable} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{16\pi s}. $$
For a parent at rest of energy $\mathsf M_0>2m_s$ and a constant identical
daughter amplitude $G_E$ in joules, take the daughters on the positive
$m_s$-shell with total $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$. The rate coefficient is
$$ \Gamma_{\rm coeff} =\frac{|G_E|^2}{32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0} \sqrt{1-\frac{4m_s^2}{\mathsf M_0^2}}\quad[\mathrm{s}^{-1}]. $$
If an energy width is named, its convention is $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma_{\rm
coeff}$ in joules. None of these coefficient statements implies an exact
survival law. The QFT-G02 postulate is a current draft carrier; its use here
retains draft status and does not imply independent acceptance.

derivations.claim: Setting $\beta_e=\beta_\mu=1$ in [F1] gives $$ \frac{d\sigma_{\rm coeff}}{d\Omega} =\frac{\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{4s}(1+\cos^2\theta). $$ Thus its values at $0$ and $\pi/2$ are respectively $\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2/(2s)$ and $\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2/(4s)$, and their ratio is $2$. The numerator has unit $\mathrm{J}^2\mathrm{m}^2$ and $s$ has unit $\mathrm{J}^2$, so each coefficient has area unit $\mathrm{m}^2$.

Integrating the same density uses $\int_{S^2}d\Omega=4\pi$ and $\int_{S^2}\cos^2\theta\,d\Omega=4\pi/3$, so $$ \sigma_{\rm coeff} =\frac{\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{4s}\left(4\pi+\frac{4\pi}{3}\right) =\frac{4\pi\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{3s}. $$ The adopted reading [A1] introduces no count or measurement record.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
For a specifically named finite tree calculation, adopt its selected formal
diagram coefficient as a **leading perturbative coefficient** with a stated
phenomenological reading. For QED, use the vertex and free-line conventions
of the current draft supplier
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]]. A particle of natural charge $q_n$ has
vertex $iq_n\gamma^a$; the electron has $q_n=-e_n$ and vertex
$-ie_n\gamma^a$. The rational fermion line is
$$ i\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}, $$
for $\mu>0$ and off-shell $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$. In Feynman gauge
the auxiliary photon line is
$$ -i\frac{h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}=i\frac{\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}. $$
For a finite matrix kernel the coefficientwise inverse in
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]] is part of the formal convention and
asserts no convergence. If a time-ordered distribution is used, use the
actual free carrier specified there; that identification is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]. The displayed pole notation does not define loop
products. In the pair-production channel below the selected muon also has
model charge $-e$, and only the photon line is internal.

For declared incoming spin probabilities, sum over declared final spin
labels, and a specified formal amplitude $\mathcal A$, adopt the
cross-section coefficient map of
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. In the center-of-momentum frame it
uses the invariant incoming flux $F$, the two-body measure $d\Phi_2$, and the
final-state factor $S_f=2$ for identical particles or $S_f=1$ for
distinguishable particles, integrated over the full labeled sphere. When
this coefficient is read phenomenologically, the initial preparation,
channel, threshold, and approximation are part of the model statement. No
universal error estimate for omitted terms is implied.

For the scalar examples, separately adopt the constant formal amplitudes
$\mathcal A=-\lambda$ for the quartic contact channel and $\mathcal G=G_E$
for the cubic parent decay, with the units and external normalization stated
at each use. Their coefficient map is the one in
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. If a rate $\Gamma$ is reported as
an energy width, the convention is explicitly $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma$; it
does not supply a survival law.

The readings above do not identify a formal coefficient with an exact
continuum cross section, probability, decay rate, or measured estimate. In
particular they do not construct an interacting continuum $S$-matrix or LSZ
limit, establish convergence of a perturbation series, bound loop or
soft-radiation effects, specify beam or detector cuts, resolve threshold
resummation, or reproduce the statistical analysis of an experiment. A
comparison with observations would require the actual apparatus, sampling,
calibration, uncertainty, and radiative-inclusiveness conditions. The
reported electron magnetic-moment measurements, including the Fan et al.
report listed in the source references, remain source-reported
empirical results and are not premises of this adoption.
